title_en: Zou Hanying v. Sun Ligen and Liu Zhen — dispute over compensation for work-related injury damages
ruling_gist_en: In the process of organizing company liquidation, if the legal representative of a company, knowing that an employee has suffered a work-related injury and is undergoing an assessment of the injury grade, fails to consider the issue of payment of benefits after the injury grade assessment, thereby causing substantial damage to the interests of the injured employee, such conduct shall be determined to constitute gross negligence and the legal representative shall bear compensatory liability in accordance with law. Other shareholders who are members of the liquidation group, if they fail to fulfill their due diligence duty of inquiry during the dissolution and liquidation of the company, shall also be determined to have gross negligence and bear joint and several compensatory liability.

full_text_en:
Zou Hanying v. Sun Ligen and Liu Zhen

— Dispute over compensation for work-related injury damages

**Ruling Summary**

Where the legal representative of a company, in the process of organizing the company's liquidation, knowingly knows that an employee has suffered a work-related injury and that a work-related injury grade assessment is underway, but fails to take into account the payment of benefits after the injury grade assessment, thereby causing significant harm to the interests of the injured employee, such conduct shall be deemed to constitute gross negligence, and the representative shall be liable for compensation in accordance with the law. Other shareholders who, as members of the liquidation group, fail to fulfill their duty of inquiry during the company's dissolution and liquidation process shall also be found to have gross negligence and bear joint and several liability for compensation.

**Plaintiff:** Zou Hanying, female, 33 years old, Han Chinese, unemployed, residing in Wannian Village, Zhenzhou Town, Yizheng City, Jiangsu Province.

**Defendants:** Sun Ligen, male, 36 years old, Han Chinese, former shareholder of Yizheng Xinwei Lighting & Electric Appliance Co., Ltd., residing in Hongye Residential Quarter, Yizheng City, Jiangsu Province.

Liu Zhen, female, 32 years old, former shareholder of Yizheng Xinwei Lighting & Electric Appliance Co., Ltd., residing in Hongye Residential Quarter, Yizheng City, Jiangsu Province.

Plaintiff Zou Hanying filed a lawsuit with the Yizheng People's Court of Jiangsu Province against defendants Sun Ligen and Liu Zhen regarding a dispute over compensation for work-related injury damages.

**Plaintiff's Allegations:** The plaintiff was an employee of the former Yizheng Xinwei Lighting & Electric Appliance Co., Ltd. (hereinafter "Xinwei Electric"). On March 23, 2007, the plaintiff was accidentally injured while working at the company. The injury was recognized as a work-related injury by the labor department, and on June 30, 2008, the Yangzhou Labor Ability Assessment Committee assessed the plaintiff's disability grade as Grade 10. After the accident, Xinwei Electric paid all of the plaintiff's medical expenses, as well as nursing fees and nutritional fees totaling RMB 3,180 from April 17, 2007 to the end of July 2007. On February 19, 2008, Xinwei Electric applied for cancellation of registration. The defendants Sun Ligen and Liu Zhen are shareholders of Xinwei Electric. The plaintiff now requests that the court order the two defendants to pay the plaintiff's work-related injury insurance benefits, including: one-time disability subsidy of RMB 6,076.8 (1,688 × 60% × 6), one-time medical subsidy for work-related injury of RMB 15,968.48, one-time employment subsidy for disability of RMB 7,427.2, wages during the period of suspension of work for medical treatment of RMB 4,771.2, and assessment fee of RMB 280; totaling RMB 34,523.68, with the two defendants bearing joint and several liability, and the defendants bearing the litigation costs of this case.

The plaintiff submitted the following evidence:

1. Work-related injury recognition decision No. Yi Lao She Gong Shang Ren Ding (2007) 255, and Labor Ability Assessment Conclusion Notice No. Yang Yi Lao Jian Tong (2008) 33, proving the plaintiff's work-related injury and its grade;
2. One copy of the plaintiff's medical record, one copy of discharge summary, and one copy of medical certificate, proving the treatment process after the injury;
3. One written guarantee by defendant Sun Ligen, proving that after the accident, Sun Ligen promised to handle the plaintiff's work-related injury matter, and that he was responsible for handling it before Xinwei Electric was cancelled;
4. One agreement concerning the resolution of nutritional fees and nursing fees for the plaintiff during the period of work-related injury, stating that defendant Sun Ligen would pay the plaintiff RMB 30 per day for nutritional fees and nursing fees starting from April 17, 2007, without specifying an end date; the agreement bore the seal of Xinwei Electric and was signed by Sun Ligen;
5. Three copies of the plaintiff's wage statements before the work-related injury, proving that the plaintiff's wages were lower than the minimum wage standard for workers in Yizheng City;
6. One copy of the application form for cancellation of Xinwei Electric obtained from the Yizheng Administration for Industry and Commerce, proving the identities of defendants Sun Ligen and Liu Zhen as shareholders and liquidators, as well as the asset status at the time of liquidation.

**Defendants' Defense:** The defendants Sun Ligen and Liu Zhen jointly argued: They acknowledge the fact that the plaintiff Zou Hanying suffered a work-related injury while working at Xinwei Electric. However, the plaintiff's work-related injury grade assessment was only made in June 2008, while Xinwei Electric was cancelled on February 19, 2008, with the liquidation process completed before that. At the time of Xinwei Electric's dissolution and liquidation, the plaintiff's work-related injury insurance benefits had not yet arisen. Therefore, the plaintiff's claim does not meet the prerequisite for applying Article 190 of the Company Law of the People's Republic of China (hereinafter "Company Law"). Consequently, the defendants' act of liquidating and cancelling the company did not harm the plaintiff's rights and interests. The defendants had no fault in the dissolution and liquidation process, and the plaintiff's request for the defendants to pay work-related injury benefits lacks factual and legal basis. They requested the court to reject the plaintiff's claim. Liu Zhen claimed she was unaware of the plaintiff's work-related injury and had no fault, and therefore should not bear joint and several liability.

The Yizheng People's Court organized cross-examination in accordance with the law. Defendants Sun Ligen and Liu Zhen had no objection to the authenticity and legality of evidence items 1, 2, 3, and 6 submitted by the plaintiff. Regarding evidence item 4, they had no objection to its authenticity but argued that after the plaintiff was discharged from the hospital, the wound healed well during the rest period, and the labor ability assessment conclusion notice was issued on June 30, 2008, after Xinwei Electric was cancelled, so the company could not have known that the plaintiff's injury had reached Grade 10 disability. Regarding evidence item 5, the defendants argued that two of the three wage statements showed wages when the plaintiff did not work full attendance, and the third showed wages for 25 days of attendance, which was insufficient to prove that the plaintiff's wage standard was lower than Yizheng's minimum standard. The defendants objected to the wage standard used in calculating the one-time disability subsidy within the compensation items, but had no objection to the calculation methods and amounts of other compensation items, although they believed that these costs should not be borne by them.

**Facts Found by the Court at First Instance**

The plaintiff Zou Hanying was an employee of Xinwei Electric. On March 23, 2007, the plaintiff was accidentally injured while working at the company. On December 4, 2007, the plaintiff's injury was recognized as a work-related injury by the Yizheng Bureau of Labor and Social Security. After the accident, Xinwei Electric paid the plaintiff's medical expenses, as well as nursing fees and nutritional fees totaling RMB 3,180 from April 17, 2007 to the end of July 2007.

Defendants Sun Ligen and Liu Zhen were shareholders of Xinwei Electric. The company was dissolved by a resolution of the shareholders' meeting and applied for cancellation on February 19, 2008.

On June 30, 2008, the Yangzhou Labor Ability Assessment Committee assessed the plaintiff's disability grade as Grade 10. On September 9, 2008, the plaintiff applied for arbitration with the labor department. On September 10, 2008, the Yizheng Labor Dispute Arbitration Committee issued a notice of non-acceptance to the plaintiff on the ground that the subject being sued was not qualified.

**Issue at First Instance:** Whether the defendants Sun Ligen and Liu Zhen should bear the plaintiff's work-related injury insurance benefits and be jointly and severally liable.

**Opinion of the Court at First Instance**

The lawful rights and interests of laborers shall be protected in accordance with the law. The plaintiff Zou Hanying suffered a work-related injury while working at Xinwei Electric and is legally entitled to work-related injury benefits. Since the employer did not participate in the work-related injury insurance pooling, the employer shall bear the work-related injury insurance benefits for the injured worker according to the relevant national standards. Because Xinwei Electric's legal personality ceased to exist upon cancellation, the plaintiff cannot sue that company as a defendant. Defendants Sun Ligen and Liu Zhen, as former shareholders of Xinwei Electric and members of the company's liquidation group, should perform their statutory duties in accordance with the law. According to Article 190 of the Company Law, members of a liquidation group who cause losses to the company or its creditors due to intentional acts or gross negligence shall be liable for compensation. In this case, the two defendants knew that the plaintiff had suffered a work-related injury, and therefore during the liquidation process should have taken into account the payment of the plaintiff's work-related injury benefits, but they omitted it, causing significant harm to the plaintiff's interests. This constitutes gross negligence, and the two defendants shall compensate the plaintiff for her losses. Therefore, the defendants' defenses are not accepted. Regarding the plaintiff's claimed amounts: one-time medical subsidy for work-related injury of RMB 15,968.48, one-time employment subsidy for disability of RMB 7,427.2, wages during suspension period of RMB 4,771.2, and assessment fee of RMB 280, to which the two defendants had no objection, these are supported. Regarding the plaintiff's claimed one-time disability subsidy of RMB 6,076.8 (1,688 × 60% × 6 months), the defendants objected to the wage standard. The court holds that according to Article 61 of the Regulations on Work-Related Injury Insurance of the State Council, "wages of the employee" refers to the average monthly wages on which social insurance premiums were paid in the 12 months prior to the accident or diagnosis of occupational disease. If the employee's wages are lower than 60% of the average wages of workers in the pooling area, 60% of the average wages of the pooling area shall be used. The plaintiff's claim does not violate the law, and is therefore supported.

Accordingly, the Yizheng People's Court of Jiangsu Province, in accordance with Article 190 of the Company Law, Article 73 of the Labor Law of the People's Republic of China, and Articles 31 and 35 of the Regulations on Work-Related Injury Insurance of the State Council, rendered the following judgment on February 16, 2009:

Defendants Sun Ligen and Liu Zhen shall, within 10 days from the effective date of this judgment, pay the plaintiff Zou Hanying a one-time disability subsidy of RMB 6,076.8, a one-time medical subsidy for work-related injury of RMB 15,968.48, a one-time employment subsidy for disability of RMB 7,427.2, wages during the suspension period of RMB 4,771.2, and an assessment fee of RMB 280, totaling RMB 34,523.68, with the two defendants bearing joint and several liability for the above amounts.

Litigation costs of RMB 663, reduced by half to RMB 331.5, shall be borne by defendants Sun Ligen and Liu Zhen.

Sun Ligen and Liu Zhen, dissatisfied with the first-instance judgment, appealed to the Yangzhou Intermediate People's Court of Jiangsu Province. Their grounds of appeal were: The first-instance judgment had unclear factual findings and improper application of the law. The appellee Zou Hanying was injured on March 23, 2007, recognized as having a work-related injury on December 4, 2007, and Xinwei Electric was cancelled on February 19, 2008, with the dissolution and liquidation process completed before that. On June 30, 2008, Zou Hanying was assessed as having a Grade 10 disability, meaning that Zou Hanying's work-related injury insurance benefits had not yet arisen at the time of Xinwei Electric's dissolution. Therefore, the appellants could not have known at the time of Xinwei Electric's dissolution and liquidation whether Zou Hanying's claimed benefits would arise, and Xinwei Electric could not have waited for Zou Hanying's benefits to arise before dissolving. Xinwei Electric dissolved and was cancelled because it could no longer continue its business. The appellants, as members of the liquidation group, did not have the fault of maliciously disposing of company property, nor did they engage in any malicious disposal. Therefore, they should not bear liability for Zou Hanying's claimed work-related injury benefits. Liu Zhen was unaware of the fact of Zou Hanying's injury and should not bear liability. They requested that the first-instance judgment be overturned.

The appellee Zou Hanying responded: The appellants Sun Ligen and Liu Zhen were aware of Zou Hanying's work-related injury and condition, and could not have been unaware of the injury grade assessment being conducted. Because the relevant authority only conducts such assessments twice a year, the assessment result had not yet been issued when Xinwei Electric was cancelled—this was merely a matter of procedure and timing. Therefore, at the time of Xinwei Electric's dissolution and liquidation, the appellants should have taken into account Zou Hanying's work-related injury benefits. However, in the actual liquidation, the appellants, as members of the liquidation group, failed to consider the benefits Zou Hanying was entitled to, causing significant losses to Zou Hanying's lawful rights and interests, and they should be liable for compensation in accordance with the law.

The Yangzhou Intermediate People's Court, upon second-instance trial, confirmed the facts found at first instance.

The issue at second instance remained: whether the appellants Sun Ligen and Liu Zhen should pay the appellee Zou Hanying's work-related injury insurance benefits and bear joint and several liability.

**Opinion of the Court at Second Instance**

According to Article 73 of the Labor Law of the People's Republic of China, laborers who suffer work-related injuries or disabilities are entitled to social insurance benefits in accordance with the law. The appellee Zou Hanying was injured on March 23, 2007 while working at Xinwei Electric, and the injury was recognized as work-related on December 4, 2007, so she is legally entitled to work-related injury insurance benefits. According to Articles 2 and 60 of the Regulations on Work-Related Injury Insurance of the State Council, employers shall participate in work-related injury insurance in accordance with the regulations and pay insurance premiums for employees. If an employee suffers a work-related injury while the employer is not covered by work-related injury insurance, the employer shall pay the expenses according to the items and standards of work-related injury insurance benefits under these Regulations. Since Xinwei Electric did not participate in the social work-related injury insurance pooling, Xinwei Electric shall bear the appellee's work-related injury insurance benefits according to the relevant national standards.

Regarding the appellants' argument that at the time of Xinwei Electric's dissolution and liquidation, the appellee's injury grade assessment result had not yet been issued and her benefits had not yet arisen, the court holds: The appellee was injured on March 23, 2007 while working, and her injury was recognized as work-related on December 4, 2007, meaning she was legally entitled to work-related injury insurance benefits from that point. The injury grade assessment result is the main basis for determining the specific content of the benefits. Although the assessment result had not yet been issued and the specific content and amount of benefits could not be determined, this does not affect the accrual of the appellee's right to benefits. Before Xinwei Electric was dissolved, Sun Ligen, as one of its shareholders, clearly knew that the appellee had suffered a work-related injury. Therefore, at the time of dissolution and liquidation, although the appellee's injury grade had not yet been assessed, Sun Ligen, as the company's legal representative and a member of the liquidation group, was aware that the appellee had been injured, the injury had been recognized as work-related, and an injury grade assessment was underway. Under these circumstances, he should have included the appellee's work-related injury insurance benefits in the company's liquidation calculations.

In summary, appellant Sun Ligen, in organizing the company's liquidation process, knew that the appellee Zou Hanying had suffered a work-related injury and that an injury grade assessment was ongoing, but failed to consider the payment of benefits after the assessment, thereby causing significant harm to the appellee's interests. This conduct clearly constitutes gross negligence. According to Article 190 of the Company Law, members of a liquidation group who cause losses to the company or its creditors due to intentional acts or gross negligence shall be liable for compensation. Accordingly, Sun Ligen shall bear liability for compensation in accordance with the law. Appellant Liu Zhen, as a shareholder of Xinwei Electric and a member of the liquidation group, failed to timely ascertain the existing fact of the appellee's work-related injury during the dissolution and liquidation process. She clearly failed to fulfill the duty of care incumbent upon a member of the liquidation group, and there is no evidence that the other member of the liquidation group, Sun Ligen, deliberately concealed the fact of the appellee's injury from her during the liquidation. Therefore, with respect to the loss of the appellee's work-related injury benefits, Liu Zhen's conduct also constitutes gross negligence, and she shall bear joint and several liability with Sun Ligen. If Liu Zhen believes that a relevant responsible party was at fault in this regard, she may, after bearing liability, seek recourse from that party in accordance with the law.

In conclusion, the grounds of appeal of the appellants Sun Ligen and Liu Zhen are untenable and are not supported. The first-instance judgment found the facts clearly and applied the law correctly, and should be affirmed. Accordingly, the Yangzhou Intermediate People's Court, in accordance with Article 153, Paragraph 1, Item (1) of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, rendered the following judgment on February 16, 2009:

Appeal dismissed, and the original judgment affirmed.

Litigation costs for the second instance of RMB 663 shall be borne by the appellants Sun Ligen and Liu Zhen.

This judgment is final.
